data.title: Ecthyma — viva
data.summary: Bacterial infections · 6 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Ecthyma** (Bacterial infections)_

**Q1. What is ecthyma?**
- Ulcerative pyoderma extending into the dermis, caused by Streptococcus pyogenes (± S. aureus); 'deep impetigo'
- Heals with scarring

**Q2. Clinical features?**
- Vesicopustule on legs of children/elderly → thick adherent grey-yellow/brown-black crust; removal shows punched-out saucer-shaped ulcer with raised indurated margin; regional lymphadenopathy common; 0.5–3 cm

**Q3. Predisposing factors?**
- Poor hygiene, malnutrition, insect bites/scabies, minor trauma, warm humid climate, diabetes, neglected excoriations, soldiers/travellers

**Q4. Differential diagnosis?**
- Ecthyma gangrenosum (Pseudomonas, neutropenic), cutaneous anthrax, leishmaniasis, insect bite reaction, pyoderma gangrenosum, vasculitic ulcer, sporotrichosis, Buruli ulcer, tungiasis

**Q5. What is ecthyma gangrenosum?**
- Pseudomonas aeruginosa septicaemia in immunocompromised/neutropenic patients — painless red macules → haemorrhagic bullae → necrotic ulcer with black eschar, anogenital/axillary; needs IV antipseudomonal therapy

**Q6. Treatment?**
- Soaks to remove crust, topical mupirocin, oral penicillin/cloxacillin/cephalexin or macrolide for 10 days; treat underlying scabies/insect bites

## Quick spotter facts
- Punched-out ulcer with adherent crust on shin — ecthyma

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Bacterial infections — ecthyma); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.15. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
